The records first set rules concerning prayer, purification, illness, journeys, and the absence of water, while also promising Gardens, pure companions, and plenteous shade to those who believe and do good works. They then warn that those who disbelieve Allah’s revelations will enter the Fire, where renewed skins make them continually taste torment. The account turns to people of the Scripture who demand a Book from heaven, recalls earlier wrongdoing, the request to see Allah plainly, worship of the calf after clear proofs, and forgiveness. It concludes that people break their covenant and disbelieve in Allah’s revelations, while Allah reveals to Muhammad in His knowledge and the angels testify.

Good works are done by believers, those who believe and do them. In the passage, believers are instructed about approaching prayer in states of drunkenness or pollution and about using clean soil if water is unavailable. Those who combine belief with good works are promised entry into Gardens with rivers, pure companions, plenteous shade, and everlasting dwelling.
are_given_to believers [in Gardens] Pure companions are promised to those who believe and do good works in the Gardens.

A dispute concerning any matter is to be referred to Allah and the messenger if the people are believers in Allah and the Last Day. People are also required to accept the messenger's judgment in disputes without dislike and with full submission.

The hypocrites are people who turn away with aversion when called to what Allah has revealed and to the messenger. Allah knows the secrets of their hearts; they are to be opposed, admonished, and addressed plainly about their souls. Believers are divided into two parties regarding them, while Allah has cast them back to disbelief because of what they earned. They desire believers to disbelieve as they do, choose disbelievers as friends instead of believers, and seek to beguile Allah. Their worship is languid and performed to be seen by people, and they are mindful of Allah only a little. They waver between believers and disbelievers, belonging fully to neither; when Allah causes them to go astray, they have no way. They receive a painful doom, are gathered with disbelievers into hell, and are in the lowest deep of the Fire with no helper. Yet those among them who repent, amend, hold fast to Allah, and make their religion pure for Allah are with the believers.

Messengers are messengers of Allah, sent to mankind with good cheer and warning. No messenger is sent except to be obeyed by Allah’s leave, and believers in Allah and the Last Day obey them by that leave. Their coming leaves mankind with no argument against Allah, whose might and wisdom frame their mission. People are told to believe in Allah’s messengers, while disbelievers may wrongly distinguish among them by believing in some and disbelieving in others. Those who believe in Allah and all His messengers without making distinctions are promised their wages from Allah, who is Forgiving and Merciful. The account closes by presenting belief in the messenger who has come with Truth from the Lord as better for mankind, while affirming that Allah possesses all that is in the heavens and earth and is Knower and Wise.

l: a straight road, Surah 4: The Women (An-Nisaa)
s: A straight road is the way by which Allah guides believers in Allah and the Last Day. It leads to Allah. Allah guides those who do what they are exhorted to do unto it, amid commands to restore deposits, judge justly, obey Allah and the messenger, and believe in the Truth. Those who believe in Allah and hold fast unto Him are guided unto Him by this straight road.

l: those shown favour by Allah, Surah 4: The Women (An-Nisaa)
s: Those shown favour by Allah are the prophets, saints, martyrs, and righteous. Allah commands restoring deposits and judging justly; those who obey Allah and the messenger are with these favoured people.

The prophets are people whom Allah has shown favour and to whom He inspires revelation. They belong to the best company alongside those who obey Allah and the messenger. The records also place them within a wider account of people receiving clear proofs, forgiveness, authority, disbelief, wrongdoing, and guidance. Most gravely, some prophets were slain wrongfully.
are_with those shown favour by Allah The righteous are among those unto whom Allah has shown favour, and those who obey Allah and the messenger are with them.

Muhammad is a messenger who receives Scripture and guidance from Allah and comes to mankind with the Truth from their Lord. He is to be obeyed as Allah is obeyed, while he is not sent as a warder over people. Believers are commanded to believe in the Scripture revealed to him, and reports of safety or fear are to be referred to him and those in authority so capable people may understand them. His message confronts a decisive response: whoever rejects or opposes the messenger after Allah’s guidance has been manifested, and follows another way, is appointed to what he has turned toward and exposed to hell. The records conclude by affirming that the messenger has come to all mankind with the Truth from Allah and that belief is better for them, though Allah possesses all that is in the heavens and earth.

Fighting is prescribed for believers in the cause of Allah. It is presented as a means to benefit oppressed people and to oppose those who fight for idols or make war against believers. It follows an earlier instruction for some people to withhold their hands, establish worship, and pay the poordue. The account distinguishes enemies by conduct: those who hold aloof, do not wage war, and offer peace are not to be opposed; those who repeatedly return to hostility, neither hold aloof nor offer peace, may be fought. Believers are urged to take precautions and advance in groups or all together.

l: the way of Allah, Surah 4: The Women (An-Nisaa)
s: The way of Allah is a cause for which believers fight, taking precautions and advancing in groups or all together. It calls people to give up the life of this world for the Hereafter; those who fight are promised a vast reward whether slain or victorious. In contrast, those who disbelieve, do wrong, and hinder others from the way of Allah are far astray, without forgiveness or guidance to a road.

Oppressed men, women, and children are portrayed as crying for deliverance from a town ruled by oppressors. Their suffering is presented as a reason to fight for the cause of Allah, while seeking a protecting friend from Allah.

l: life of this world, Surah 4: The Women (An-Nisaa)
s: is_scat comfort The world is one of the realms for which Allah gives reward. Whoever desires the reward of the world is directed to Allah, with whom that reward is found.

Hereafter is a realm beyond this world, presented as better for those who ward off evil. It receives such people with a better outcome than worldly life, whose comfort is scant by comparison. People who fight in the way of Allah may receive reward there. Allah possesses the reward of both the world and the Hereafter, so those who seek worldly reward are reminded that reward in both realms is with Allah.

The Qur'an is from Allah and calls its hearers to ponder. It urges believers to take precautions and advance together or in proven groups, then affirms Allah alone and a certain Day of Resurrection, presenting Allah as wholly true.

l: Day of Resurrection, Surah 4: The Women (An-Nisaa)
s: The Day of Resurrection is the certain, doubtless day on which Allah gathers everyone. It is a day of gathering for all and a day of judgment, when judgment occurs between the parties. On that day, Allah judges between believers and disbelievers and gives the disbelievers no way against the believers. Those who pleaded for wrongdoers in the life of the world will have no stated defender with Allah.

take_in_death oppressed people [while they wrong themselves] Angels take in death those who wrong themselves and ask what they were engaged in. They question those who claim oppression in the land about why they did not migrate.

l: believer killed by mistake, Surah 4: The Women (An-Nisaa)
s: A believer killed by mistake is addressed through required penance for the killer. The killer must free a believing slave and pay blood-money to the slain person’s family, unless the family remits it as charity. If the killer lacks the means, the required penance becomes fasting for two consecutive months. The record also notes that different provisions apply when the victim belongs to a hostile people or a people under covenant.
is spacious [such that migration is possible] Allah’s earth is described as spacious enough for those who are oppressed to migrate within it.

Peace is presented as the better course in relations among believers and within marriage. Believers are told to accept those who stand apart, do not fight, and offer peace, and not to deny the belief of someone offering peace for worldly gain. In matters concerning women, orphans, and children, the text calls for just dealing and says Allah knows every good done. When a woman and her husband fear ill treatment or desertion, they may establish peace; the text concludes that peace is better.
The unit permits killing certain hostile people who refuse peace and continue hostility, but forbids killing a believer except by mistake and condemns intentional killing of a believer.
Mistaken killing requires freeing a believing slave, and in specified cases also requires paying blood-money to the slain person’s family. A person without the means must fast two consecutive months.
has_as_reward hell as an eternal punishment [when directed against a believer] Whoever intentionally kills a believer is threatened with hell forever, Allah’s wrath and curse, and an awful doom.
Blood-money must be paid to the family of a believer killed by mistake unless they remit it as charity. It must also be paid to the people of a person from a covenant people who is killed by mistake.
The penance for mistaken killing includes freeing a believing slave, and when the killer lacks the means, fasting two consecutive months. The text calls this a penance from Allah.

Migration is undertaken for Allah’s cause. Those oppressed in the land are urged to migrate when able, and migrants are promised refuge and abundance in the earth. Whoever leaves home as a fugitive unto Allah and His messenger but is overtaken by death has a reward incumbent on Allah, who is Forgiving and Merciful.

l: fighting in Allah's way, Surah 4: The Women (An-Nisaa)
s: Fighting in Allah’s way is described through believers who strive with their wealth and lives. They are ranked above those who remain sedentary and receive a great reward, degrees of rank, forgiveness, and mercy. The account also connects striving to migration for Allah’s cause: leaving home brings refuge and abundance, and death during that flight makes reward incumbent on Allah.

l: hell as an eternal punishment, Surah 4: The Women (An-Nisaa)
s: is hell [for the intentional killer of a believer, forever] Intentional killing of a believer is described as resulting in hell forever. This punishment is accompanied by Allah’s wrath, curse, and an awful doom.

has_fixed_times fixed times [enjoined on believers] Worship may be curtailed during travel when believers fear attack. It is arranged in alternating groups with arms and precautions, followed by remembrance of Allah; in safety, worship is to be observed properly at fixed times.

l: people who deceive themselves, Surah 4: The Women (An-Nisaa)
s: People who deceive themselves are treacherous and sinful, hide from men, hold secret nighttime conferences displeasing to Allah, receive worldly defense from men, and are not harmed by Muhammad. They conceal themselves from people but not from Allah.

l: grace of Allah, Surah 4: The Women (An-Nisaa)
s: is_infinite infinite [toward Muhammad] Allah's grace and mercy prevent a party from misleading Muhammad, and Allah's grace toward him is described as infinite. Allah's grace is also associated with a vast reward for those who seek His good pleasure through almsgiving, kindness, and peace-making.

l: those who believe and do good works, Surah 4: The Women (An-Nisaa)
s: Those who believe and do good works are brought into Gardens of Paradise beneath which rivers flow. They abide there forever, and male and female believers enter without being wronged even the dint in a date-stone.

l: People of the Scripture, Surah 4: The Women (An-Nisaa)
s: People of the Scripture are a religious group with desires that believed in Jesus son of Mary before his death. They ask for an actual Book to descend from heaven. Their history is presented through earlier actions: asking Moses to show Allah plainly, choosing the calf after clear proofs, breaking their covenant, disbelieving in Allah’s revelations, and saying they slew Jesus son of Mary. Though forgiveness was given after the calf, disbelief and wrongdoing are said to receive neither forgiveness nor guidance. The account closes by telling them not to exaggerate in their religion and to say nothing about Allah except the truth.

Female orphans are included among those concerning whom the Scripture gives decree. The text addresses those to whom what is ordained for female orphans is not given, although they desire to marry them.

l: reward of the world, Surah 4: The Women (An-Nisaa)
s: The reward of the world belongs to Allah and is linked with the Hereafter. The record says those who desire it should know it is with Allah, who is ever Hearer and Seer, within a passage urging just treatment of female orphans and weak children.

l: a painful doom, Surah 4: The Women (An-Nisaa)
s: is_received_by those who were scornful and proud [as punishment] A painful doom is the punishment for those who were scornful and proud.
belongs_to Allah [all] The hypocrites seek power through disbelievers by choosing them as friends instead of believers. The unit states that all power belongs to Allah.

When victory comes to believers from Allah, the hypocrites claim to be with them. The hypocrites also speak of having mastery over disbelievers and protecting believers when disbelievers have success.
